What I do

Reporting and analysis, from the routine to the forensic.

Ten services, grouped by the job you need doing — build something new, stop doing it by hand, or find out why the numbers don't add up.

Build it Automate it Investigate it
Group 1 · Build it

New reports, built around the questions you actually ask.

Not a template with your logo on it. I start from the decisions you need to make and work backwards to the report that answers them.

Power BI — automated reports

Fully automated reports in the modern PBIP project format: source-connected, version-controlled and set to refresh on their own.

  • Refreshes on a schedule, hands-off
  • Version-controlled and maintainable
More on Power BI

Power BI — static reports

Polished, point-in-time reports for a board pack, a client or a one-off review — built clean and delivered ready to share.

  • Consistent month to month
  • PDF or deck, meeting-ready
See a sample

Excel reports & models

Reliable Excel reporting — formulas you can trust, a layout anyone can pick up, and no hidden columns holding it together.

  • Auditable, documented formulas
  • Totals that reconcile
More on Excel
Group 2 · Automate it

Stop rebuilding the same report every week.

If a person has to remember to do it, it will eventually be late or wrong. The fix is to take the person out of the loop.

Report automation

I connect the sources once and set the report to refresh and deliver itself on a schedule — no exports, no copy-paste, no reminders.

  • Runs whether anyone remembers or not
  • Alerts you when a refresh fails
What would it save?

Consolidation & data merges

Five spreadsheets, three systems and a CSV export turned into one clean dataset that everything else can be built on.

  • One source of truth
  • Duplicates and key mismatches resolved

Data trends

See the direction of travel — what's rising, falling or shifting — early enough to act on it rather than react to it.

  • Seasonality separated from real change
  • Like-for-like comparisons
Group 3 · Investigate it

When the numbers don't agree, find out why.

This is the forensic end of the work: two systems disagreeing, a report that never quite ties, or money going somewhere nobody can explain.

Cross-examination

I put your numbers side by side across systems, periods and records to confirm they actually agree — and hold up when someone challenges them.

  • Record-level, not just totals
  • A repeatable check, not a one-off

Finding discrepancies

Track down the mismatches between systems and reports — and explain exactly why they happened, not just that they did.

  • Root cause, in plain English
  • A fix so it stops recurring

Finding losses

Surface leakage, missed revenue, duplicate costs and quiet errors that are draining money without anyone noticing.

  • Quantified, so you can prioritise
  • Evidence you can take to a supplier

Bank statement income reports

Turn raw bank statements into clear, categorised income and cashflow reports — ideal for affordability, lending, or a true picture of the money.

  • Categorised income and outgoings
  • Recurring items identified

Insights & interpretation

Beyond the numbers: what they actually mean, what's driving them, and the decision they point to. A report nobody can interpret isn't finished.

Any other data question

If it involves data and a question you need answered, it's worth asking. Tell me what you're trying to work out and I'll tell you whether I can help.

How a piece of work runs

Same shape, whether it's an afternoon or an ongoing report.

You'll know the price and the deliverable before anything starts.

Step 1

Audit

I map your data, sources and the question you need answered — and agree what "done" looks like.

Step 2

Build

I build the report, model or analysis, checking the numbers as I go so you can trust the output.

Step 3

Automate

Where it's recurring, I set it to refresh and deliver itself — no manual rebuild.

Step 4

Support

I stay on hand to adapt and extend it as your questions and data change.

Not sure which of these you need?

Describe the problem in plain terms — "two systems don't match", "this report eats my Mondays" — and I'll tell you the shortest way to fix it.
